name.text: Alternate Interior Angles Theorem and Exercise_sec2

questiontext.text:
Alternate Interior Angles Theorem:

When a line (called a transversal) crosses two parallel lines, the pair of angles that lie on opposite sides of the transversal but inside the parallel lines are called alternate interior angles (shaded in green). These angles are always equal.

In the diagram below:

  • Parallel lines: AB and CD
  • Transversal: XY
  • The alternate interior angles are the shaded ones
[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-1, 7, 8, -1], axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Define points for parallel lines var A = board.create('point', [0,5], {name:'A', size:2, fixed:true}); var B = board.create('point', [7,5], {name:'B', size:2, fixed:true}); var C = board.create('point', [0,2], {name:'C', size:2, fixed:true}); var D = board.create('point', [7,2], {name:'D', size:2, fixed:true}); // Draw parallel lines AB and CD var lineAB = board.create('line', [A, B], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2}); var lineCD = board.create('line', [C, D], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2}); // Define points for transversal var X = board.create('point', [1,0], {name:'X', size:2, fixed:true}); var Y = board.create('point', [4,6], {name:'Y', size:2, fixed:true}); // Draw transversal XY var transversal = board.create('line', [X,Y], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2, dash:2}); // Intersection points of transversal with parallel lines var O1 = board.create('intersection', [lineAB, transversal, 0], {name:'O₁', size:2}); var O2 = board.create('intersection', [lineCD, transversal, 0], {name:'O₂', size:2}); // Highlight alternate interior angle at O1 (angle AO1X) board.create('angle', [A, O1, X], { radius: 0.6, name: ' ', type: 'sector', fillColor: 'lightgreen', fillOpacity: 0.6, strokeColor: 'green', strokeWidth: 1 }); // Highlight alternate interior angle at O2 (angle DO2Y) board.create('angle', [D, O2, Y], { radius: 0.6, name: ' ', type: 'sector', fillColor: 'lightgreen', fillOpacity: 0.6, strokeColor: 'green', strokeWidth: 1 }); // Highlight alternate interior angle at O1 (angle YO1A) board.create('angle', [Y, O1, A], { radius: 0.6, name: ' ', type: 'sector', fillColor: 'lightred', fillOpacity: 0.6, strokeColor: 'red', strokeWidth: 1 }); // Highlight alternate interior angle at O1 (angle XO2D) board.create('angle', [X,O2, D], { radius: 0.6, name: ' ', type: 'sector', fillColor: 'lightblack', fillOpacity: 0.6, strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 1 }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Given the size of angle \(\angle AO_1XO_2 is x \), we can show that \(\angle O_1O_2 D is also x \) using the following proof steps:

Proof:

1. \(\angle AO_1X = \angle YO_1B\) because they are vertically opposite angles.
2. \(\angle YO_1B = \angle DO_2Y\) because they are corresponding angles when lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) are parallel.
Therefore, \(\angle AO_1X = \angle DO_2Y\).

This proves that alternate interior angles are equal when a transversal cuts two parallel lines.


Suppose \(\angle AO_1X = {@angle_alt@}^\circ\), what will be the measure of \(\angle DO_2Y\) ?
